messages:
Alex: Heads up — we saw a small skew in priority routing during the last canary. Some cohort users were routed to the cost-optimized pool even though their tenant-level quota had a higher priority. Noticed it around 17:03 UTC.
Maria: ugh. Is that the same tie-breaker bug we thought was fixed?
Sam: I dug quick logs. Looks like when two routes tie on priority we fall back to hash mod of tenant_id, which is fine generally, but our hash seed changed after the last rollout (runtime config bump).
Jin: seed changed because of the config schema migration — we default to zero if seed missing. Some older snapshots didn't include seed -> fallback zero -> many tenants colliding.
Alex: Okay that explains the cluster. How many affected? severity?
Sam: ~0.3% of requests in the canary window. SLOs fine, but it broke expected quota isolation for a couple of teams.
Maria: For rollout safety: can we add a preflight that checks for missing seed fields and rejects or warns? Also a console warning for any pending snapshots without seed.
Jin: I'd prefer non-blocking warning + auto-fill. Migration path: if seed missing, generate per-tenant stable seed derived from tenant_id (HMAC), store back to snapshot in background. No runtime interrupt.
Alex: That sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) short-term: patch runtime to prefer explicit seed over hash fallback, 2) mid-term: snapshot migration job.
Sam: Agree. Patch in runtime is tiny: when seed absent, compute HMAC(tenant_id, global_key) instead of zero. But we need to ensure global_key is stable across clusters (use config-store).
Maria: global_key exists in config-store but it's scoped per-region. We must ensure consistent across canary pool. Could leak if different keys across regions -> different routing.
Jin: use a rollout-safe global_key: add a flag in runtime-config that pins the HMAC key for tie-breaker migrations. That key will be rolled via canary with the migration job.
Alex: Telemetry: let's add a metric 'routing.tie_breaker.source' with labels {seed_source=explicit|derived|legacy_zero} and a daily alert if derived > 0.1% during rollouts.
Sam: I'll add the metric and a console dashboard tile showing distribution by seed_source and affected quota anomalies.
Maria: For console UX: show a tiny bang icon next to any snapshot missing seed with tooltip: "derived seed applied — consider migrating snapshot" and link to migration runbook. Keeps support questions down.
Jin: Runbook sketch: 1) schedule migration job (low QPS), 2) backfill snapshot seeds, 3) validate by checking routing.tie_breaker.source == explicit for sample tenants, 4) disable derived fallback.
Alex: Who owns the migration job and safety checks? Sam for telemetry + validation, Jin for migration job implementation, Maria for console UX and runbook text. I'll triage and create task IDs.
Sam: ok assigned — I'll instrument and create dashboard. Will add anomaly alert to paging if tie_breaker.source==legacy_zero spikes >0.5% in 15m.
Jin: I'll prototype the migration in staging, want to test with >50k synthetic tenants to ensure no perf regression.
Maria: UX note: make the console copy clear that derived seeds are deterministic and safe, else customers will be confused.
Alex: timeline: patch runtime today (hotfix to canary), telemetry + dashboard tomorrow, migration job next week, console UX next week. Sound realistic?
Sam: yep. I'll push runtime metric PR now and add the alert.
Jin: I'll open migration RFC and start prototype.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/runtime-canary-2026-03-23-1 to canary pool (20% capacity). Checks: unit tests passed, smoke ok.
Alex: thanks. After deploy, monitor routing.tie_breaker.source and quota mismatch logs for 30m. Ping channel with status. :thumbsup:
Maria: Thanks everyone — I'll add the console tooltip copy to the PR for review.
Sam: Patch landed to staging. Will post link to PR in a sec.
Jin: migration RFC: https://r.redwood/runbooks/migrations/tie-breaker-seed (draft)
Alex: Great work. We'll debrief tomorrow if anomalies persist.
